drinks.name: Espresso
drinks.header: A concentrated shot with a rich, golden crema.

difficulty.reason: Dialing in grind and pulling a balanced shot take practice.

recipe.waterGuidance: Fill the machine reservoir; target 36 g of brewed espresso rather than measuring water into the portafilter.
steps: Grind 18 g of coffee finely and dose it into the portafilter.
Distribute, tamp evenly, and lock in the portafilter.
Set the machine to about 93°C and pull about 36 g of espresso in 25–30 seconds. Taste and adjust the grind next time.

light.flavor: Light roasts often taste brighter and more acidic, with fruit or floral notes.
light.extraction: As a starting point, use more extraction energy because the less-developed beans tend to give up flavor less readily in a short espresso shot.
light.temperatureExplanation: Start at 94°C, 1°C hotter than Medium, to add extraction energy during the brief brew.
light.grindExplanation: Use a fine ~150–400 µm grind, slightly finer than Medium, to expose more coffee to the water.

steps: Grind 18 g of coffee finely and dose it into the portafilter.
Distribute, tamp evenly, and lock in the portafilter.
Set the machine to about 94°C and pull about 36 g of espresso in 25–30 seconds.

medium.flavor: Medium roasts often balance sweetness, acidity, and body.
medium.extraction: As a starting point, use the published recipe as the moderate reference for a balanced espresso extraction.
medium.temperatureExplanation: Keep the established Medium target of 93°C as the balanced reference point.
medium.grindExplanation: Keep the established fine ~200–500 µm grind as the balanced reference point.

dark.flavor: Dark roasts often emphasize cocoa, caramelized, and bittersweet flavors with lower perceived acidity.
dark.extraction: As a starting point, use gentler extraction because the more-developed, porous beans can release roast-forward flavors quickly, although coffees still vary.
dark.temperatureExplanation: Start at 90–91°C, cooler than Medium, to limit harsh or bitter roast flavors during the short brew.
dark.grindExplanation: Use a slightly coarser fine ~300–600 µm grind so extraction proceeds more gently than with Medium.

steps: Grind 18 g of coffee to a slightly coarser fine setting and dose it into the portafilter.
Distribute, tamp evenly, and lock in the portafilter.
Set the machine to about 90–91°C and pull about 36 g of espresso in 25–30 seconds.

drinks.name: Latte
drinks.header: Espresso softened with plenty of silky steamed milk.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and controlled milk steaming.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe and pour it into a cup.
Steam 180 mL of milk to about 60°C, creating glossy microfoam.
Pour the milk into the espresso, finishing with a thin layer of foam.

drinks.name: Cappuccino
drinks.header: A balanced espresso and milk drink with a generous foam cap.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and a generous, even milk foam.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe and pour it into a cup.
Steam 120 mL of milk to about 60°C, adding more air than for a latte.
Pour the milk over the espresso, keeping a generous foam layer on top.

drinks.name: Pour-over
drinks.header: A clear, flavorful cup made by slowly pouring water over coffee.

difficulty.reason: Requires a steady pour and attention to brew time.

steps: Rinse the filter and add 15 g of medium-fine coffee.
Pour 30 mL of 94°C water to wet all the grounds; wait 30 seconds.
Pour the remaining 210 mL slowly in circles. Aim to finish draining in 3–4 minutes.

light.flavor: Light roasts often taste brighter and more acidic, with fruit or floral notes that a clear pour-over can highlight.
light.extraction: As a starting point, use more extraction energy because less-developed beans tend to release flavor less readily during percolation.
light.temperatureExplanation: Start at 96°C, hotter than Medium, to help water extract the light roast evenly.
light.grindExplanation: Use a fine-to-medium-fine ~400–700 µm grind, finer than Medium, to expose more surface area.

steps: Rinse the filter and add 15 g of fine-to-medium-fine coffee.
Pour 30 mL of 96°C water to wet all the grounds; wait 30 seconds.
Pour the remaining 210 mL slowly in circles. Aim to finish draining in 3–4 minutes.

medium.flavor: Medium roasts often balance sweetness, acidity, and body in a clear pour-over.
medium.extraction: As a starting point, use the published recipe as the moderate reference for balanced percolation.
medium.temperatureExplanation: Keep the established Medium target of 94°C as the balanced reference point.
medium.grindExplanation: Keep the established medium-fine ~500–800 µm grind as the balanced reference point.

dark.flavor: Dark roasts often emphasize cocoa, caramelized, and bittersweet flavors with lower perceived acidity.
dark.extraction: As a starting point, use gentler extraction because more-developed, porous beans can release roast-forward flavors quickly, although coffees still vary.
dark.temperatureExplanation: Start at 90°C, cooler than Medium, to reduce the chance of harsh or bitter flavors.
dark.grindExplanation: Use a medium ~700–1000 µm grind, coarser than Medium, to slow extraction through the coffee bed.

steps: Rinse the filter and add 15 g of medium-ground coffee.
Pour 30 mL of 90°C water to wet all the grounds; wait 30 seconds.
Pour the remaining 210 mL slowly in circles. Aim to finish draining in 3–4 minutes.

drinks.name: French press
drinks.header: An easy immersion brew with a rounded, heavier body.

difficulty.reason: Immersion brewing needs only a timed steep and careful pressing.

steps: Add 16 g of coarse coffee to the press and pour in 240 mL of 94°C water.
Stir gently, cover, and steep for 4 minutes.
Press the plunger slowly and pour right away.

light.flavor: Light roasts often taste brighter and more acidic, with fruit or floral notes and a rounded immersion body.
light.extraction: As a starting point, use more extraction energy because less-developed beans tend to release flavor less readily during the steep.
light.temperatureExplanation: Start at 96°C, hotter than Medium, to help the immersion draw flavor from the light roast.
light.grindExplanation: Use a medium-coarse ~800–1100 µm grind, finer than Medium but still suitable for the press filter.

steps: Add 16 g of medium-coarse coffee to the press and pour in 240 mL of 96°C water.
Stir gently, cover, and steep for 4 minutes.
Press the plunger slowly and pour right away.

medium.flavor: Medium roasts often balance sweetness, acidity, and body, reinforced by French press immersion.
medium.extraction: As a starting point, use the published recipe as the moderate reference for a balanced steep.
medium.temperatureExplanation: Keep the established Medium target of 94°C as the balanced reference point.
medium.grindExplanation: Keep the established coarse ~1000–1400 µm grind as the balanced reference point.

dark.flavor: Dark roasts often emphasize cocoa, caramelized, and bittersweet flavors with lower perceived acidity and a heavy body.
dark.extraction: As a starting point, use gentler extraction because more-developed, porous beans can release roast-forward flavors quickly, although coffees still vary.
dark.temperatureExplanation: Start at 90°C, cooler than Medium, to keep the long immersion from emphasizing harsh or bitter flavors.
dark.grindExplanation: Use a coarse-to-very-coarse ~1200–1600 µm grind, coarser than Medium, for a gentler steep and clean pressing.

steps: Add 16 g of coarse-to-very-coarse coffee to the press and pour in 240 mL of 90°C water.
Stir gently, cover, and steep for 4 minutes.
Press the plunger slowly and pour right away.

drinks.name: Americano
drinks.header: Espresso lengthened with hot water for a gentler cup.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot followed by controlled dilution.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe.
Add 150 mL of dilution water at about 85°C to a mug.
Pour the espresso into the water and serve.

drinks.name: Macchiato
drinks.header: A traditional espresso marked with a small spoonful of milk foam.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and a small amount of textured milk foam.

steps: Prepare the full double-shot Espresso recipe in a small cup.
Steam a little milk to about 60°C and spoon 5–10 mL of foam on top.

drinks.name: Turkish coffee
drinks.header: Finely ground coffee simmered in a cezve and served unfiltered.

difficulty.reason: Slow heating and watching the rising foam prevent boiling over.

steps: Add 70 mL of room-temperature water, 7 g of extra-fine coffee, and optional sugar to a cezve. Stir before heating.
Heat slowly until the foam rises; remove before it boils over.
Pour gently into a small cup and let the grounds settle before sipping.

light.flavor: Light roasts often taste brighter and more acidic, with fruit or floral notes that remain vivid in this concentrated cup.
light.extraction: As a starting point, heat slowly and steadily so the less-developed coffee has enough contact and energy before the foam rises.
light.temperatureExplanation: Keep the starting water unchanged at about 20°C because room-temperature water and controlled heating define the Turkish method.
light.grindExplanation: Keep the grind unchanged at extra-fine ~50–200 µm because suspended powder-fine coffee defines the method.

steps: Add 70 mL of room-temperature 20°C water, 7 g of extra-fine coffee, and optional sugar to a cezve. Stir before heating.
Heat slowly and steadily so the light roast extracts before the foam rises; remove before it boils over.
Pour gently into a small cup and let the grounds settle before sipping.

medium.flavor: Medium roasts often balance sweetness, acidity, and body in the concentrated Turkish preparation.
medium.extraction: As a starting point, use the published slow-heating method as the moderate reference for balanced extraction.
medium.temperatureExplanation: Keep the starting water unchanged at about 20°C because room-temperature water and controlled heating define the Turkish method.
medium.grindExplanation: Keep the grind unchanged at extra-fine ~50–200 µm because suspended powder-fine coffee defines the method.

dark.flavor: Dark roasts often emphasize cocoa, caramelized, and bittersweet flavors with lower perceived acidity in this concentrated cup.
dark.extraction: As a starting point, heat gently because the more-developed, porous coffee can release roast-forward flavors quickly, although coffees still vary.
dark.temperatureExplanation: Keep the starting water unchanged at about 20°C because room-temperature water and controlled heating define the Turkish method; gentler heating supplies the control.
dark.grindExplanation: Keep the grind unchanged at extra-fine ~50–200 µm because suspended powder-fine coffee defines the method.

steps: Add 70 mL of room-temperature 20°C water, 7 g of extra-fine coffee, and optional sugar to a cezve. Stir before heating.
Heat gently and watch closely as the foam rises so the dark roast does not overheat; remove before it boils over.
Pour gently into a small cup and let the grounds settle before sipping.

drinks.name: Mocha
drinks.header: A comforting latte with chocolate blended in.

difficulty.reason: Requires espresso, chocolate mixing, and controlled milk steaming.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe and stir 20 g of chocolate sauce into it until smooth.
Steam 180 mL of milk to about 60°C and pour it over the chocolate espresso.
Stir gently and serve.

drinks.name: Flat white
drinks.header: A small milk drink where the espresso stays prominent.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and fine, lightly aerated milk.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe in a small cup.
Steam 140–160 mL of milk to about 60°C with very fine microfoam.
Pour the milk into the espresso with only a thin foam layer.

drinks.name: Iced latte
drinks.header: Fresh espresso poured over cold milk and ice.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and simple cold assembly.

steps: Fill a tall glass with 120 g of ice and add 180 mL of refrigerated milk.
Prepare the Espresso recipe.
Pour the espresso over the milk and ice; stir to combine.
